title: The Septuagint’s order
principle: The Greek Old Testament in its own order — Law, Histories, Poetic books, Prophecies — with the deuterocanon in place, then the New Testament.

source.name: The order of Rahlfs’s Septuaginta, as printed in A New English Translation of the Septuagint (NETS, 2007), contents
source.licence: The order is a fact; no NETS text is used

caveat: Read in Brenton’s English Septuagint where it holds the book, and in the King James otherwise. 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) is not in the Septuagint and is not here; “2 Esdras” in Rahlfs is Ezra–Nehemiah.
sequence: 1–4 Reigns: Samuel and Kings under the Greek names.
1 Esdras, then “2 Esdras” — Ezra and Nehemiah as one book.
Esther; the Greek book weaves in the Additions, read here after it.
The Prayer of Manasses, among the Odes printed after the Psalms.
The Twelve first among the Prophecies, in the Greek order.
Baruch, then Lamentations, then the Letter of Jeremiah (Baruch 6 in the King James).
Susanna before Daniel, as the Greek prints it; the Song of the Three stands inside Daniel 3.
